evidence: Mau Mau from Within (6 thesis citations), credited to Donald L. Barnett and Karari Njama, is catalogued under Barnett, Don, 1930-1975. Donald L. and Don identify the same author.
The sole work, A Rebelião dos Marinheiros (6), is by Avelino Bioen Capitani; Biden is a misspelling in the citation.

Christelle Fischer-Bovet's USC publication list includes all three titles: Army and Society in Ptolemaic Egypt, A Challenge to the Concept of Decline, and Est-il facile de conquérir l’Égypte? All 8 listed thesis citations are hers; Ch is an abbreviation.

Os bancos do Brasil (5) is Bernardo de Souza Franco's book; the 1839 and 1841 speeches (1 each) explicitly name him in their titles. The 2014 article Investigações sobre a ditadura são travadas pelas Forças Armadas (1), credited to Lucas Ferraz and Bernardo Mello Franco, belongs to the modern journalist. LC share: 7/8.

Brown credits From Slavery to the Cooperative Commonwealth (6) to Alexander Gourevitch; the publisher credits Labor and Republican Liberty (2011; 1) to Alex Gourevitch of Brown. Both are the same political theorist.

The sole title, Between Damnation and Starvation (6), is catalogued by CiNii with John P. Greene as the statement of responsibility and Greene, John Carrick as the author heading, directly bridging the differing names.

Inside the Confederate Government (5) is the diary of Robert Garlick Hill Kean. Dear Marraine, 1917–1919 (1) concerns Robert Winthrop Kean's First World War service, as confirmed by American Ancestors. These are two people; LC share: 5/6.

An Introduction to the Medieval Bible (5) is by Frans van Liere, the published name of Franciscus A. van Liere. Columbia's contents credit Biblical Exegesis Through the Twelfth Century (1) to him. The Practice of the Bible row (1) embeds that same chapter citation in cited_authors, rather than identifying a different van Liere.

Almanak/Almanaque da Província de São Paulo para 1873 are spelling and edition variants of the same work. CiNii credits the 1985 facsimile to Antonio José Baptista de Luné and Paulo Delfino da Fonseca. All 6 listed thesis citations refer to this work; Baptiste is a spelling error.

The sole title, The Puritans and the Church Courts in the Diocese of York, 1560–1642 (6), is explicitly credited to Ronald A. Marchant in its contemporary Cambridge journal review. Robert is a citation error.
